extracted.intended_audience: SEC reporting professionals, corporate accountants, corporate counsel, CFOs and preparers of Form 8-K/registration/proxy filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on when and how SEC financial statement and pro forma reporting requirements apply to acquisitions, dispositions, and probable acquisitions of businesses (S-X Rule 3-05, Rule 11-01, Form 8-K and related instructions). Intended to help registrants determine filing triggers, required disclosures, timing, and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination whether a business has been acquired
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination of whether a business has been acquired should be made in accordance with the guidance set forth in § 210.11-01(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The acquisition of a business encompasses the acquisition of an interest in a business accounted for by the registrant under the equity method or, in lieu of the equity method, the fair value option.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related businesses treated as single acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquisitions of a group of related businesses that are probable or that have occurred subsequent to the latest fiscal year-end must be treated as if they are a single business acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required financial statements of related businesses may be presented on a combined basis for any periods they are under common control or management. Businesses are 'related' if: (i) they are under common control or management; (ii) the acquisition of one is conditional on the acquisition of each other; or (iii) each acquisition is conditioned on a single common event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exceptions — real estate operations and wholly-held businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: This section does not apply to a real estate operation subject to §210.3-14 or a business which is totally held by the registrant prior to consummation of the transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: When pro forma financial information must be filed (S-X Rule 11-01(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Pro forma financial information must be filed when any of specified conditions exist (e.g., significant acquisition in most recent fiscal year or interim period; consummation or probable significant acquisition after latest balance sheet; securities offered to security holders of a significant business; disposition of a significant portion of a business not fully reflected in registrant statements; roll-up transactions; registrant previously part of another entity and autonomous presentation necessary; other transactions material to investors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerated conditions (from the rule): (1) significant business acquisition during most recent fiscal year or subsequent interim period; (2) consummation or probable significant acquisition after date of most recent balance sheet; (3) securities being registered are to be offered to security holders of a significant business or proceeds applied to purchase a specific significant business; (4) disposition of a significant portion of a business has occurred or is probable and not fully reflected in registrant statements; (5) [Reserved]; (6) pro forma required for roll-up transactions per §229.914; (7) registrant was part of another entity and presentation necessary to reflect autonomous operations; (8) consummation of other transactions has occurred or is probable for which pro forma would be material.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-X Rule 3-05(a) — filing financial statements of acquired business when significant
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05(a) requires a registrant to file the financial statements of the acquired business when it is significant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform significance tests after determining an acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a registrant determines it has acquired a business, it must perform the significance tests in chapter 3 to determine its reporting requirements for the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision tree applies only to acquisitions that have been consummated and are significant; different requirements apply for probable acquisitions and acquisitions by shell companies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K filing timing for consummated acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For a consummated acquisition of a business, file Form 8-K announcing the acquisition within 4 business days of consummation and amend the Form 8-K within 71 calendar days of the initial Form 8-K due date to include the acquired business' historical financial statements and pro forma information (when required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If audited financial statements required by Item 9.01 are not available by the 4th business day, estimate timing and file Item 2.01 on Form 8-K, then amend with Item 9.01 information within the extra 71-calendar-day window (subject to exceptions such as shell companies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thresholds for significance — business vs assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Different significance thresholds apply depending on whether the transaction involves a business or assets: acquisitions/dispositions of businesses — 20% significance threshold; acquisitions/dispositions of assets (not businesses) — 10% threshold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The amendments to Article 11 increased disposition threshold from 10% to 20% for businesses (effective fiscal years after Dec 31, 2020). However, legacy 10% threshold remains for asset acquisitions/dispositions that do not meet the definition of a business.

rubrics_metrics.name: When registration/proxy statements must include acquired business financials
rubrics_metrics.description: If an acquired business is >50% significant (and for some cases >20%), the registration or proxy statement should include the historical financial statements of the acquired business and pro forma financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision-tree language: If acquired business is >50% significant, include historical financial statements and pro forma information. If >20% significant, also include historical financial statements and pro forma information when filing a registration or proxy statement after consummating the acquisition. (Different rules apply for probable acquisitions — see related entries.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of consummation of an acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Consummation of a business acquisition generally coincides with a closing that involves the legal transfer of title to property or securities evidencing ownership in the business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consummation may involve transfer of legal ownership of equity securities or obtaining control by contract or agreement. The consummation date is the date on which title passes or ownership or control of the interest in the business is obtained. The instructions to Item 2.01 of Form 8-K identify possible acquisitions such as a purchase, lease, exchange, merger, consolidation, succession or other acquisition transaction. Acquisitions do not include construction/development of property or acquisition of materials for that purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'related' businesses for reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05 requires acquisitions of related businesses to be evaluated for significance as though they were acquired in a single acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Businesses are 'related' if: under common control or common management; acquisition of one is conditional on acquisition of another; or each acquisition is conditioned on a single common event. Related acquisitions are combined for significance testing if they occur within any one fiscal year plus the interim period after the latest fiscal year-end but before filing the audited financial statements for that fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements for unrelated businesses significant in the aggregate
rubrics_metrics.description: If consummated and probable acquisitions are greater than 50% significant in the aggregate when filing a registration statement or certain proxy materials, the registrant provides pro forma financial information for the aggregate impact and, in some cases, financial statements for individual acquisitions that otherwise would not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no Form 8-K filing requirement to report acquisitions of unrelated businesses that are significant in the aggregate; the aggregate-triggered disclosures apply to registration/proxy filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probable acquisition does not trigger Form 8-K Item 9.01 filing
rubrics_metrics.description: The probable acquisition of a business does not trigger the filing of the target’s financial statements on a Form 8-K; the Form 8-K filing requirement is triggered only upon consummation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, certain registration statements (including Forms S-4 or F-4) require financial statements for a probable significant business acquisition under S-X Rule 3-05.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to treat an acquisition as probable for registration/proxy purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: If at the time a registrant files a registration statement or mails certain proxy materials it is probable that it will acquire a business, the registrant must perform the significance tests in chapter 3 to determine reporting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a probable-to-be-acquired business is >50% significant, include historical financial statements and pro forma information in the registration statement or certain proxy materials. Even if individually less than 50%, aggregate significance of consummated + probable acquisitions >50% may create requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: How likelihood ('probable') of acquisition is determined
rubrics_metrics.description: S-X Rule 3-05 does not define 'probable'; SEC staff views public announcement as strong evidence that an acquisition is probable. Registrants should consider facts and circumstances and legal advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important factors: progress of negotiations; economic and legal penalties for failure to consummate (costs incurred to date); significance of required regulatory approvals. Helpful steps to consider (common in closing): execute preliminary notice of interest; meet with senior executives; execute confidentiality/exclusivity agreements; execute letters of intent; conduct due diligence; execute agreement in principle; obtain board/shareholder approvals; submit regulatory filings. Codification note: consummation considered probable when registrant's financial statements alone would not provide investors adequate information to make an investment decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquisitions arising from events (not transactions) — probability assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A business acquisition can occur when one entity obtains control of another through an event (e.g., expiration of noncontrolling rights) rather than a transaction; determining whether such an acquisition is probable is fact-dependent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally, the further in the future the control is expected to be obtained, the less likely the acquisition is probable at the filing date and the less relevant the target's current financial information is to investors. Registrants should reassess likelihood as facts change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma filing requirements for disposition of a significant business
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant disposes of a business that is >20% significant, S-X Article 11 requires the registrant to provide pro forma financial information reflecting the impact of the disposition, unless the impacts are fully reflected in the registrant's financial statements (e.g., presented as discontinued operations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legacy Article 11 had a 10% disposition threshold; amendments raised it to 20% for businesses effective after Dec 31, 2020. The 10% threshold remains for dispositions of assets that are not businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K Item 2.01 — information required for completion of acquisition/disposition of assets
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant or any consolidated subsidiary has completed the acquisition or disposition of a significant amount of assets (not in ordinary course), disclose: (a) date of completion; (b) brief description of assets; (c) identity of persons from whom assets were acquired or to whom sold and material relationships; (d) nature and amount of consideration and formula if material relationship disclosed; (e) identity of source(s) of funds if material relationship exists (subject to confidentiality procedure); (f) if registrant was a shell company immediately before transaction, the information required if filing a Form 10 registration reflecting all classes of registrant's securities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No information need be given for transactions between wholly-owned subsidiaries or redemption/acquisition of securities in public markets by the issuer or its wholly-owned subsidiary. Definitions for acquisition and disposition are provided in Item 2.01 instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form 8-K General instruction — filing deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: A report on Form 8-K is required to be filed or furnished upon the occurrence of any one or more of the events specified; unless otherwise specified, a report is to be filed or furnished within four business days after occurrence of the event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If event occurs on a weekend or holiday, the four business day period starts on the next business day. Special timing rules apply for certain Items (e.g., Item 5.08, Item 7.01 / Item 8.01 and Regulation FD references).

rubrics_metrics.name: Item 9.01 — Financial statements and exhibits triggered by significant business acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Item 9.01 requires the filing of financial statements of businesses or funds acquired, pro forma financial information, and copies of the plans of acquisition or disposition as exhibits when required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An acquisition or disposition of a significant business triggers the filing of a Form 8-K for domestic registrants subject to periodic filing requirements. Item 9.01 requires providing registrant pro forma financial information after a significant (20% level) acquisition or disposition of a business or real estate operation (S-X Rule 11-01(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregation rule for Item 2.01 — related businesses and aggregates
rubrics_metrics.description: The aggregate impact of acquired businesses is not required to be reported pursuant to Item 2.01 unless they are related businesses (or related real estate operations/funds) and are significant in the aggregate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relatedness is determined per S-X Rule 3-05(a)(3). If related and significant in the aggregate, combined reporting and presentation rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision tree for whether Form 8-K is required for an acquisition
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a stepwise decision process: Is the registrant domestic (or foreign filer electing Form 8-K)? Do the assets acquired constitute a business per S-X Rule 11-01(d)? Is the significance >20% per S-X Rule 1-02(w) tests? Are audited financial statements required by Item 9.01 currently available? Will Item 9.01 information be available within 4 business days plus 71 calendar days after acquisition?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If registrant is domestic, assets constitute a business, and significance >20%: file Form 8-K containing Item 2.01 on or before the 4th business day after the acquisition; estimate when Item 9.01 will be filed and amend within the 71-calendar-day window. If audited statements will not be available within the extension window, consult advisers and consider requesting SEC no-action relief. Note: 71-day extension is not available to shell companies (e.g., SPACs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign private issuers (FPIs) — different filing obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: FPIs are not required to file periodic reports on a Form 8-K or to file proxy solicitation materials unless they elect to use domestic periodic filing forms; absent that election, filing of a registration statement is the only circumstance in which FPIs are required to file financial statements of a significant acquired or probable-to-be-acquired business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 6 provides additional guidance on acquisitions by FPIs and of foreign entities.
